title: Erlebnisse
welcome: This book is the paper half of A2.1. Every topic gets two facing pages: the **left page** teaches — tables, diagrams, the few rules that matter — and the **right page** is yours to write on.
It carries on from the A1 books. Words you learned there are not taught again; where a topic builds on something from A1, a small note brings it back.
Work with a pencil and say every German word out loud as you write it. When a page has a **Listen** code, scan it with your phone camera to hear the German.

The answers are at the back. Do a whole page first, then check, and circle what you got wrong — those circles are next week’s revision. Tick an **I can** line only when you could do it tomorrow without the book.

spreads.title: Ich bin gefahren
spreads.subtitle: Moving and changing: the Perfekt with sein
spreads.hook: Went, came, stayed, fell asleep: verbs that move you or change you take sein.

learn.title: An object turns it into haben
learn.text: Ich *bin* nach Köln gefahren (I travelled). Ich *habe* das Auto gefahren (I drove the car): with a thing after it, the same verb takes haben.

blocks.text: In the plural the noun gets an -n too: den Kinder*n*, den Freunde*n*. Not when it already ends in -n or -s: den Frauen, den Autos.

blocks.title: man is not a man
blocks.text: *man* means “you, people” in general: Hier darf *man* nicht parken. Wie sagt *man* das auf Deutsch? It takes the er-form: man *sagt*, man *kann*.

learn.title: alle or alles?
learn.text: *alle* are people — they: Alle *sind* da. *alles* is things — it: Alles *ist* fertig.
